sections.h2: Where is Duluth and how does the hillside shape the city?
sections.html:
Duluth is a port city on the western tip of Lake Superior and the county seat of St. Louis County. It covers 71.69 square miles of land, and the Census Bureau estimates 88,330 residents as of July 1, 2025, which makes it one of Minnesota's largest cities.

The city climbs a steep hillside from the lakeshore to the plateau above, and the population hugs the shoreline, so Duluth runs mostly southwest to northeast. The weather station at Sky Harbor Airport on Minnesota Point sits at 607 feet, while Duluth International Airport on top of the hill is at 1,427 feet. Skyline Parkway runs along the ridge from above the Gary and New Duluth area to Lester Park, and neighborhoods such as Piedmont Heights and Bayview Heights sit up top with long views. Over the hill, the Miller Hill Mall area and the big-box strips along the Miller Trunk Highway corridor form a separate retail center.

For a seller, the steep streets and elevation changes make the exact address matter more than it does in a flat suburb.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Duluth?
sections.html:
The Ojibwe name for the area is Onigamiinsing, or Misaabekong. The city takes its name from Daniel Greysolon, Sieur du Lhut, the first known European explorer of the St. Louis River, in 1679. Fur traders worked the Fond du Lac area through the early 1800s, and the American Fur Company set up its headquarters at present-day Fond du Lac in 1817.

The 2020 census counted 86,697 people, which ranked Duluth fifth among Minnesota cities. By land area it is second in the state, behind only Hibbing. Duluth and Superior, Wisconsin, share a metropolitan area known as the Twin Ports.

Duluth serves as the regional center for health care, higher education, retail and business services across northeastern Minnesota and nearby parts of Wisconsin and Michigan. The Census Bureau recorded $3.1 billion in health care and social assistance receipts in the city for 2022.

  • The Port of Duluth handles about 35 million short tons of cargo and nearly 900 vessel visits a year, including coal, iron ore, grain, limestone and wind turbine parts.
  • The University of Minnesota Duluth enrolled 9,253 students in 2024, Lake Superior College 5,607 and the College of St. Scholastica 2,930.
  • Tourism leans on Canal Park, the Aerial Lift Bridge, the North Shore drive and access to the Boundary Waters.
  • Maurices, the women's clothing chain, is headquartered here.

Most public school students attend Duluth Public Schools, Independent School District 709. The Proctor Public School District covers a small part of southwest Duluth, and Duluth Edison Charter Schools serve kindergarten through grade 8.

sections.h2: How does Duluth weather affect an older house?
sections.html:
Duluth has a humid continental climate moderated by the lake, and winters are long. Highs stay at or below 32 degrees for about 100 days a year, temperatures fall to 0 or below on 38 nights, and snow cover lasts from late November to early April. Average snowfall is 90.2 inches, and lake-effect storms can leave a foot or more near the shore while places 50 miles inland get much less.

The first freeze usually arrives around September 30 and the last around May 14. The record low is minus 41 degrees, set in 1885, and July days average about 78 degrees. A house here carries a heavy load from snow, ice and freeze-thaw cycles, so roofs, gutters, foundations and insulation draw attention from buyers and inspectors.

sections.html:

In 2024 there were 1,195 single-family listings and 1,033 sales. Foreclosures in Duluth ran 16 in 2020, 8 in 2021, 30 in 2022, 34 in 2023 and 20 in 2024. The Census Bureau puts the owner-occupied rate at 59.4 percent, the median value of owner-occupied homes at $242,700 and median gross rent at $1,087. Median household income is $68,807, and the poverty rate is 16.8 percent.

sections.h2: Which Duluth housing and building codes apply to a sale?
sections.html:
Duluth keeps its housing rules in the city's Legislative Code, and several chapters touch a sale.

  • Chapter 29A covers housing, property maintenance and rental licensing. The Life Safety Division of the Fire Department administers it, and it adopts the 2012 International Property Maintenance Code.
  • Chapter 30 covers abandoned property and inoperable vehicles.
  • Chapter 50, the Unified Development Code, is the zoning code.
  • Chapter 10 adopts the Minnesota building code, and the 2020 edition took effect in Duluth on March 31, 2020.

Rental owners should know that about 17,633 units held active rental licenses in 2024 and that 39.4 percent of households rent. Construction Services and Inspections is at 411 West First Street, Room 100, and the phone number is 218-730-5240. If the house had a fire, note that Duluth withholds fire escrow funds under Minnesota Statutes 65A.50, so ask the city what applies before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: Can a Duluth vacation rental permit transfer to a buyer?
sections.html:
No. Duluth requires a city permit to rent any part of a property on Airbnb, Vrbo or similar sites, and existing vacation dwelling units are not transferable to another owner. An Interim Use Permit lasts six years or until ownership changes, whichever comes first.

There are three kinds of permit. An Accessory Home Share Permit applies when the owner lives in the building and allows stays of 1 to 29 nights, with up to 4 guests in 2 bedrooms. An Accessory Vacation Dwelling Unit, Limited Permit covers an owner-occupied homestead rented for 2 to 7 nights, to a maximum of 21 nights a year. Interim Use Permits allow 2 to 29 nights, a local property manager and no more than 9 guests. Those permits are subject to a city-wide cap outside the form districts, and the city says the current waiting list is expected to take several years. A buyer who wants income from short stays should confirm eligibility with Planning at 218-730-5580 before closing.

sections.h2: What does St. Louis County handle in a Duluth sale?
sections.html:
The St. Louis County Recorder and Registrar of Titles handles deeds and certificates of title. About two-thirds of documents recorded there involve abstract property and about one-third involve Torrens property, so ask your title company which kind you have. The county does not offer legal advice or help preparing documents.

Minnesota's state deed tax is 0.33 percent of net consideration under Minnesota Statutes 287.21, so a sale at the 2024 median price of $295,000 carries about $974 in tax. You also owe the buyer written disclosure of material facts under Minnesota Statutes 513.55.

County property tax is due May 15 and October 15. The 2026 second half has passed, so the next payment is May 15, 2027. Value appeals start with the assessor, then the city board of appeal and equalization in April or May, then the county board in the last two weeks of June, and a Minnesota Tax Court petition must be filed by April 30 of the year the tax is payable.

sections.h2: What are your choices for selling a house in Duluth?
sections.html:
You can list through an agent, sell the house yourself, or take a direct cash offer, and the best route depends on repairs, timing and what the house is used for.

With average time on market at 19 days in 2024, a well-prepared Duluth listing can move quickly. A cash sale suits a vacation rental owner who cannot transfer a permit, a landlord ending a license, a house with winter damage, or an estate that needs to close without repairs. Compare any offer with the median sale price, ask for the terms in writing, and keep your tax, permit and disclosure paperwork in one folder.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Duluth Airbnb with its permit?
faqs.a: No. The city says existing vacation dwelling units cannot transfer to another owner, and an Interim Use Permit ends when ownership changes or after six years. A buyer must apply under the city's rules, and Planning at 218-730-5580 can explain the current cap and waiting list.

faqs.q: What was the median home sale price in Duluth in 2024?
faqs.a: The median single-family sale price was $295,000, up from $282,350 in 2023. Average time on market was 19 days, according to the city's 2024 Housing Indicator Report.

faqs.q: What happens to insurance money on a fire-damaged Duluth house?
faqs.a: Duluth withholds fire escrow funds under Minnesota Statutes 65A.50. Contact Construction Services and Inspections at 218-730-5240 to learn what applies to your property before you sign a sale agreement.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Duluth property value?
faqs.a: Start by contacting the St. Louis County assessor. If you are not satisfied, appear before the city board of appeal and equalization in April or May, then the county board in the last two weeks of June, and file in Minnesota Tax Court by April 30 of the year the tax is payable.

faqs.q: Does winter make it harder to sell a house in Duluth?
faqs.a: Snow cover usually lasts from late November to early April, and the average snowfall is 90.2 inches, so showings happen in tough conditions. Clear walks and roofs, keep the driveway plowed and have heating and insulation records ready, since buyers look closely at winter performance.
